I have seen CSS injection in few security tutorials (one of them is https://learn.snyk.io/lessons/xss/javascript/)
From what I understand, it's very important to protect against this attack because the attacker can change the whole view of the website via styling (and actually show on screen whatever they want).
I just thought it might be good idea to add it to the list following the word "like". like this:

> Verify that a Content Security Policy (CSP) response header is in place that helps mitigate impact for XSS attacks like HTML, DOM, **CSS**, JSON, and JavaScript injection vulnerabilities.

Btw, it's achieved by using the [style-src directive](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Content-Security-Policy/style-src).

@tghosth It can be addressed using `style-src` without including `unsafe-inline` in the Content Security Policy. 

Including CSS XSS within ASVS will, hopefully, push the browsers to include a way to inline css securely (i.e. `<style integrity="...">...`).
